notes: Named Zosyn by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18: "I prefer generic names, but for combination products that can be a problem. Call it Zosyn." A brand name is a valid R name, as MEGX and MDMA are, so it needs no display name. "The PK should be labelled piperacillin": the drug is Zosyn, its curve is labelled piperacillin, and tazobactam is not plotted. Earlier decision of the same day: tazobactam is not a drug of its own, being given only in combination; the products are listed as "Piperacillin/tazobactam" and "Ceftolozane/tazobactam", each dosed in the units of its FDA label. This row and the next replace the planned stand-alone tazobactam. No new paper: stanpumpR's piperacillin (Kong 2025, R/drugs_piperacillin.R) already takes a dose of the product and plots piperacillin, tazobactam not plotted. The change: list it as Piperacillin/tazobactam and dose it in the Zosyn label's units, g of the combined product for adults (2.25, 3.375 and 4.5 g; 3.375 g q6h is 13.5 g a day, 12.0 g piperacillin + 1.5 g tazobactam, 8:1) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (90 mg/kg from 2 to 9 months, 80 piperacillin + 10 tazobactam; 112.5 mg/kg over 9 months), in place of today's mg pip-tazo. Renaming the drug piperacillin to Zosyn leaves links naming piperacillin to be mapped to it. Zhang 2021 and Chandorkar 2015, the largest tazobactam fits in nlmixr2lib, are ceftolozane-tazobactam fits and belong to the next row.

Ceftolozane/tazobactam. Named Zerbaxa by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-18 ("Use Zerbaxa and Avycaz too", after naming Zosyn); its curve is labelled ceftolozane. The same decision of that day: dosed in the Zerbaxa label's units, g of the combined product for adults (1.5 g = 1 g ceftolozane + 0.5 g tazobactam, 2:1, q8h for cIAI and cUTI; 3 g for HABP/VABP) and mg/kg of the combined product for children (30 mg/kg = 20 ceftolozane + 10 tazobactam; 60 mg/kg; 75 mg/kg for HABP/VABP; each up to the adult dose). Plot ceftolozane, 2/3 of the dose, as piperacillin's product unit carries 4/4.5 (its doseProducts block); tazobactam not plotted. Source: Zhang 2021 (PMID 32949031, in the archive, read in full on the 2026-11-18 run for its tazobactam half), which fits both components; nlmixr2lib files its ceftolozane model as Zhang_2021_ceftolozane (968 participants). Label: DailyMed setid 70ac1d90-eff3-4f0b-9f46-5846c571b32f (May 2026). The model's volumes rise with the infection (pneumonia about doubles them). The open infection decision: decided 2026-11-18: an infection field, built in PR #861 (R/infection.R; categories none, cUTI, cIAI, pneumonia, pneumoniaVentilated, other; default none, Shafer 2026-11-24). Weekly run 2026-11-19: BLOCKED on the [decision] above, now the only thing in the way. Zhang 2021 (PMID 32949031) read in full on the PDF; every ceftolozane number is in Table 2 and its printed equations (no supplement needed): CL 4.84 L/h x (CrCL/100)^0.701 x 1.18^cUTI x 1.43^cIAI x 0.32^ESRD; Vc 9.23 L x (WT/70)^0.684 x 1.25^cUTI x 1.59^cIAI x 2.00^pneumonia x 2.14^other x 1.30^ESRD; Q 3.13 L/h; Vp 4.78 L x (WT/70)^0.484; CrCL by Cockcroft-Gault; reference healthy (28.6% of the 968, renal impairment without infection included). [decision] for Shafer, asked 2026-11-25: the category mapping (none = healthy; cUTI, cIAI as fitted; both pneumonia categories x 2.00 on Vc, non-ventilated an extrapolation; other = Zhang other infection); ESRD not applied (no field). MIC line free 4 mg/L (CLSI/EUCAST P. aeruginosa), no band: no ceftolozane MBC distribution found ([decision] whether to accept no band, as cefepime). Norvir. Kept as a drug of its own by Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-23: "I would leave ritonavir in as a model, because the pharmacokinetics of CYP3A4 inhibition are interesting." Though given today almost only as a booster (Kaletra, Paxlovid, boosted darunavir and atazanavir), it is labelled alone. Its own disposition is nonlinear (it inhibits and induces its own CYP3A4 metabolism), which a source must describe. nlmixr2lib holds seven ritonavir models, all fitted in patients taking it as a booster (the largest Mensing 2017, 2,348 adults with hepatitis C on paritaprevir/ritonavir); whether a pick describes ritonavir's own time-dependent disposition is to be read.
